diagnostic_evidence.quote:
By stationarity, there exist $\lambda_i, \mu_i \ge 0$
with $\lambda_i u_i = 0$ and $\mu_i(u_i - C_{k(i)}) = 0$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated pairing (lambda_i with u_i = 0, mu_i with u_i = C_{k(i)}), stationarity of the Lagrangian gives G_i - s_i*rho = lambda_i - mu_i, not mu_i - lambda_i as displayed. The displayed equation is false as written: e.g., for N=2, y=(1,2), epsilon/100=0.1, Omega=I, C large, the optimum alpha=(0,0.35), alpha*=(0.35,0), b=-rho=1.45 gives G_1 - rho = 0.2 > 0 while mu_1 - lambda_1 = -lambda_1 <= 0, so no lambda,mu >= 0 satisfy it. The paper's KKT table is correct (alpha_k=0 implies tau_k <= -rho; alpha_k=C_k implies tau_k >= -rho), so the text's claim that complementary slackness applied to the displayed equation yields the table does not follow as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Swap the multipliers on the right-hand side: G_i - s_i*rho = lambda_i - mu_i, matching the stated complementarity pairing and the correct KKT table.
issues.overall_effect: Only the intermediate stationarity display is wrong; the KKT table and everything downstream (working sets, bias recovery, shrinking criteria, convergence argument) are correct and unaffected.
issues.title: Sign error in the KKT stationarity equation (lambda_i and mu_i interchanged)
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol correction fixes it; the section's substantive content (the KKT table) is already correct and no downstream claim or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The optimal threshold $-\rho$ lies in the interval
$[\tau_{j^*}, \tau_{i^*}]$ (from~\eqref{eq:mvp} and Table~\ref{tab:kkt}).

issues.failure_explanation: From the KKT table, every i in I_up has tau_i <= -rho (alpha_k=0 implies tau_k <= -rho; alpha_k*=C_k implies tau_{N+k} <= -rho) and every j in I_down has tau_j >= -rho (alpha_k=C_k implies tau_k >= -rho; alpha_k*=0 implies tau_{N+k} >= -rho). Hence at the optimum tau_{i*} = max_{I_up} tau <= -rho <= min_{I_down} tau = tau_{j*}, the opposite of the displayed chain. Counterexample: N=2, y=(1,2), epsilon/100=0.1, Omega=I, C=0.1 has optimum alpha=(0,0.1), alpha*=(0.1,0) with tau=(1.0,1.7,1.2,2.1), tau_{i*}=1.2 < 1.7=tau_{j*} and valid multipliers -rho in [1.2,1.7]; the displayed chain 1.2 >= -rho >= 1.7 is unsatisfiable. The shrinking section uses the same reversed orientation. The midpoint fallback is unaffected since (tau_{i*}+tau_{j*})/2 lies in the true interval [tau_{i*}, tau_{j*}].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the chain to tau_{i*} <= -rho <= tau_{j*} (equivalently state -rho in [tau_{i*}, tau_{j*}] at convergence); the midpoint formula then lies inside the certified interval.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed bound is false in exactly the degenerate situation the remark addresses; the midpoint bias fallback, the algorithm's bias step, and the freezing criteria (which compare tau_k against tau_{j*}, tau_{i*} in the correct directions) remain valid.
issues.title: Reversed inequality chain in the degenerate-case bias bounds
issues.why_classification: A two-symbol sign flip restores correctness; the practical fallback and all dependent claims survive, so no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
If
$\Delta^{\mathrm{full}} > \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$, a frozen variable
violates KKT: reset $\Aactive = \{1,\ldots,N\}$, $\Afrozen = \emptyset$,
update $\tau$ from~\eqref{eq:reconstruct}, and continue.

Finite termination to
$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}$-optimality follows
from standard results~\cite{Fan2005, Chang2011}.

issues.failure_explanation: The reconstruction/unshrinking block is placed after \EndFor, yet its reset branch says 'continue outer loop' and no outer loop exists. When Delta^{full} > epsilon_tol after the main loop breaks — a reachable event, since the shrinking criteria can freeze a variable that later violates KKT — the algorithm resets A_active but then falls through to the bias computation and \Return, returning a solution that fails its own epsilon_tol-optimality certificate. The prose in 'Reconstruction and Unshrinking' specifies the intended reset-and-continue behavior, but the pseudocode does not implement it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Wrap the main iteration loop together with the reconstruction/check/reset block in an outer loop so that a failed full-KKT check re-enters working-set selection over the full active set, exactly as the 'Reconstruction and Unshrinking' prose specifies; no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's input-output contract (return an epsilon_tol-optimal solution) is not delivered whenever unshrinking would trigger; the convergence claim of finite termination to epsilon_tol-optimality is unsupported for the algorithm as written. All per-iteration updates, the bias fallback, and the reconstruction check itself are unaffected.
issues.title: Algorithm alg:smo: unshrinking 'continue outer loop' has no outer loop, so the solver can return an uncertified solution
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local control-flow restructuring fully specified by the paper's own prose; it preserves every guarantee and loses no mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For the symmetric-kernel variant (m2) with $a = +1$, $P \succeq 0$ is preserved and the same
guarantees apply.

issues.failure_explanation: The premise is false: Omega*_{kℓ} = K(x_k, -x_ℓ) need not be PSD. For the RBF kernel with x_1=1, x_2=-1, Omega* = [[e^{-4γ},1],[1,e^{-4γ}]] has eigenvalue e^{-4γ}-1 < 0. The conclusion can also fail for a general Mercer kernel: for K(u,v) = uv + (u²+u)(v²+v) (PSD with feature map phi(t)=(t,t²+t)) and x_1=1, x_2=2, Omega* = [[-1,2],[-2,8]] is not even symmetric, so Omega_s and P are not symmetric PSD. The conclusion does hold for kernels satisfying K(x,-x') = K(-x,x') (e.g., RBF), via the symmetrized feature map psi(x) = (phi(x)+phi(-x))/sqrt(2) giving Omega_s = (1/2)<psi,psi> ⪰ 0 — not via the stated argument.

failure_location.quote:
For $a = +1$ (even symmetry), $\Omega_s \succeq 0$
follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis K(x,-x') = K(-x,x') for all x,x' (e.g., RBF/translation-invariant kernels) or restrict m2 to such kernels, and replace the justification with the symmetrized-feature-map argument Omega_s = (1/2)<psi,psi> ⪰ 0.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee that for m2 with a=+1, P ⪰ 0 is preserved and the same convergence guarantees apply is unjustified and false for non-even kernels; the m2 a=+1 guarantee is valid only under an additional hypothesis the paper does not state.
issues.title: False justification that Omega_s is PSD for a=+1 (Omega* is not PSD in general; the conclusion needs an evenness hypothesis)
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new (standard) argument plus an added hypothesis, and the advertised generality of the m2 a=+1 guarantee is reduced; the conclusion itself survives for the paper's RBF setting, so no global proof architecture is lost.
